Arsenal face an anxious wait over the fitness of first-choice goalkeeper David Raya after the Spaniard suffered a shoulder injury during Saturday's 2-2 Premier League draw at Newcastle United.

The 31-year-old looked in noticeable discomfort before being forced off in the 69th minute at St James' Park, leaving deputy Kepa Arrizabalaga to see out the closing stages.

Mikel Arteta's side had initially taken control through Eberechi Eze's first-half opener before quickfire strikes from Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw turned the contest on its head after the interval.

Noni Madueke eventually struck a 78th-minute equaliser to rescue a share of the spoils and move the Gunners six points clear at the summit, yet Raya's premature exit overshadowed the comeback.

Speaking after the full-time whistle, Arteta viewed the result as two points dropped rather than one gained and admitted his goalkeeper's setback is a genuine concern.

Industry observers note that "Unfortunately, he had to come off, which is not good news," the Arsenal manager said via Arsenal Insider. "He will have an MRI assessment tomorrow, but at the moment I don't know.".

Raya's availability is now in serious doubt ahead of a pivotal week at the Emirates Stadium, with Arsenal hosting Borussia Dortmund in the Champions League on Tuesday before welcoming title rivals Manchester City on November 29.

Should the scan confirm a spell on the sidelines, Arrizabalaga will be thrust into the starting lineup for two of the club's most demanding fixtures of the campaign.

The three-time Premier League Golden Glove winner has made 32, 38 and 37 league appearances across the past three seasons, and any lengthy absence could be detrimental, despite Arsenal's broader sturdiness out of possession.

Former Premier League midfielder Jamie Redknapp believes losing Raya for any extended period would represent a seismic blow to Arsenal's title defence.

Speaking on Sky Sports News, the pundit labelled the Spaniard the best goalkeeper in the English top flight and questioned whether his deputy can match those lofty standards.

"David Raya is the one player that is irreplaceable in that Arsenal team," Redknapp stated.

"Kepa Arrizabalaga is not up to the level of him – I think he struggles in the Premier League – he's now going to have to play some games. That's going to be difficult for him.".

Redknapp added that Raya's absence will change everything for the Gunners in the short term, leaving Arteta desperately hoping Sunday's scan delivers encouraging news.

Published: 15:41 EST, 20 November 2026 | Updated: 23:53 EST, 20 November 2026.

Zohran Mamdani squared off with New York media and now the city's mayor will need a few months to recover.

As he revealed Friday while announcing prepares to replace Rikers Island jail, Mamdani was playing in a soccer match against the local press corps at an indoor pitch in lower Manhattan when he tore his right Achilles tendon. Consequently, Mamdani is now using crutches and a walking boot, which he expects to be in for the next six to eight weeks.

'I scored a goal soon after getting on the pitch and I forgot that I was 35,' Mamdani told gathered media on Friday at City Hall, where he was forced to rely on crutches.

Mamdani hopes to be back playing soccer again in nine months.

In a recent development, local media may not be to blame here. As Mamdani told the New York Post, he arrived late to the game and began playing without properly stretching. What's more, the Post reported that Mamdani was overheard asking his police guards which reporter tackled him, only to be told he went down untouched.

Despite Mamdani's injury, team City Hall beat the local media, 8-4.

According to recent reports, as he revealed Friday while announcing looks to close Rikers Island, Mamdani was playing  against the local press corps when tore his Achilles. Now he's in a boot (pictured).

Zohran Mamdani and wife Rama Duwaji are seen during a Brazil-Morocco World Cup match.

It has been revealed that born in Uganda and raised in Manhattan's Morningside Heights neighborhood, Mamdani played cricket and soccer in his youth. He even suited up for Bowdoin College's JV team during his days at the Maine school. Then later, as an adult, he became a shareholder of Spanish second-division club Real Oviedo.

But his biggest impact on the sport came over the summer, when Fresh York welcomed thousands of tourists for the World Cup action at MetLife Stadium in nearby East Rutherford, New Jersey.

According to recent reports, upset with ticket prices for the matches, Mamdani organized more than 100 free watch parties around the city. The events were well attended and helped locals engage with the tournament even though no actual matches were played in Newly introduced York.

Zohran Mamdani, center, joined by, from left, United States soccer star Tim Weah NYC World Cup Czar Maya Handa, and Newly introduced York council member Yusef Salaam back in May.

'We said from the beginning that the World Cup belongs to New Yorkers. This summer, we proved it,' Mamdani said in a statement. 'In the most international city on earth, you didn't need thousands of dollars to be part of the world's game.

'A kid in Corona, a nurse in Bay Ridge and a small business owner in Little Haiti could all celebrate together — for free or at a price they could afford,' he continued. 'That's what we mean when we talk about a city for the many.

'This summer, strangers became neighbors on Open Streets and in free Fan Fests across the city because government made room for people to come together. And long after the confetti is swept away, New Yorkers will keep what we built: safer streets, faster buses, stronger protections, closer neighbors and the memory of a summer when the whole world felt at home here.'.

Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1715 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation. Despite progress in standardization, current target-setting approaches remain weakened by methodological problems, including inaccurate emissions accounting, excluded emissions sources and limited comparability across companies. More importantly, many corporate targets are disconnected from the real-world sectoral transitions required to meet the Paris Agreement’s temperature goal. Drawing on evidence from four editions of the Corporate Climate Responsibility Monitor and recent literature, we argue that target-setting frameworks should place greater emphasis on systemic changes in business models, technologies and value chains. We propose transition targets as a practical complement to traditional greenhouse gas reduction targets. These targets would incentivize, guide and measure progress towards sector-specific milestones, such as electrification, low-carbon material uptake and the phase-out of emissions-intensive technologies. Embedding transition targets in accountability standards, and eventually in regulation, could help close the gap between corporate climate commitments and real-world action. It would also align corporate target-setting with the physical transition benchmarks introduced by the Paris Agreement’s Global Stocktake. The scientific community has a key role in developing robust, actionable frameworks for corporate decarbonization.

Çelik pulled from Türkiye XI with left hamstring tightness as Kalulu is already out

⏱️ ~2 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Zeki Çelik was withdrawn from Türkiye's starting line-up in Bordeaux after feeling tightness in the same left thigh muscle he injured in October.
  • Zeki Çelik’s international week ended before kick-off in Bordeaux.
  • Sources indicate that an Emirhan Topçu own goal and a goal from Eli Junior Kroupi put France ahead.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Zeki Çelik was withdrawn from Türkiye's starting line-up in Bordeaux after feeling tightness in the same left thigh muscle he injured in October. With Pierre Kalulu already sidelined, Juventus face tests that could leave them without both main right-sided defenders for Venezia and Omonia.

Zeki Çelik’s international week ended before kick-off in Bordeaux. The Juventus full-back was named in Türkiye’s starting line-up for Sunday’s Nations League match against France. His left hamstring tightened up as he went through the warm-up. He was taken out of the matchday squad as a precaution. Barış Alper Yılmaz started in his place.

Sources indicate that an Emirhan Topçu own goal and a goal from Eli Junior Kroupi put France ahead. Abdülkerim Bardakcı scored a late reply for Türkiye. The result left France top of Nations League Group A1 with 13 points. They are through to the quarter-finals, which are due next March.

Recent findings suggest that çelik now returns to Turin for tests at J|Medical. Those results will decide how Juventus line up at the back after the international break.

The location is what worries Juventus. Çelik was substituted at half-time in the 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes. His scans took place on the morning of Friday 23 October. He began a rehabilitation programme straight away and was expected back after the November break.

Tuttosport counted him among Spalletti’s first returning players, alongside Vicario and Gatti. The paper placed the Bordeaux problem in the biceps femoris of his left thigh. That is the same area as the October injury.

Çelik had only just returned after weeks out. That is why the warm-up incident has raised fears of a relapse. No diagnosis has yet been confirmed.

Juventus were already without Pierre Kalulu. He picked up the injury in the game against Fiorentina. He began treatment and was withdrawn from the France squad. Sky Sport Italia expected him to be out for about three weeks. That would rule him out of both the Venezia and Omonia matches.

If Çelik’s problem proves to be a relapse, Spalletti could be without both of his main right-sided defenders for those two games. The schedule offers little room for recovery. The Omonia match is the second of four games in 12 days.

It has been revealed that the league position adds pressure. After 11 rounds Juventus are seventh in Serie A with 18 points. Their record reads five wins, three draws and three defeats.

Venezia visit Turin first, at 12:30 on 22 November in round 12 of Serie A. Omonia then come to the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November in the Europa League league phase.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Seye Omidiora | 22 Nov 2026 03:18, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 03:18.
  • Crystal Palace winger Ismaila Sarr has confirmed that he is in discussions over a upcoming contract at Selhurst Park after putting Liverpool's summer transfer interest behind him.
  • The 28-year-old Senegal international was keen on a switch to Anfield before the Eagles reportedly rejected a £50m offer from the Merseyside giants.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Seye Omidiora | 22 Nov 2026 03:18, Last updated: 22 Nov 2026 03:18.

Crystal Palace winger Ismaila Sarr has confirmed that he is in discussions over a upcoming contract at Selhurst Park after putting Liverpool's summer transfer interest behind him.

The 28-year-old Senegal international was keen on a switch to Anfield before the Eagles reportedly rejected a £50m offer from the Merseyside giants.

Liverpool had been assessing alternatives to primary target Bradley Barcola before eventually meeting Paris Saint-Germain's £123m asking price.

Despite the frustration of seeing a high-profile move collapse, Sarr insists he remains settled in South London and is open to agreeing improved terms on his current deal that runs until 2029.

Speaking to BBC Sport, the former Watford attacker admitted he naturally gave serious thought to what joining one of world football's biggest clubs would mean for his career.

However, Sarr stressed that he is no longer dwelling on the past and is solely focused on returning from a groin injury that has restricted him to just two Premier League substitute appearances this term.

According to recent reports, "Today, that chapter is behind me," Sarr remarked. "I've always believed that you can't move forward if you're constantly looking in the rear-view mirror.".

Addressing his long-term future with the club, the winger confirmed: "Yes, there have been discussions with the club. For now, I prefer to let those conversations happen privately and concentrate on football.".

Sarr netted 21 goals across all competitions last season to help Palace lift the Conference League trophy and the board are keen to reward his stature in the squad.

When Sarr completes his recovery, he will return to work under new head coach Thomas Frank following the dismissal of Pierre Sage.

The former Brentford and Tottenham Hotspur manager endured a chastening start to his tenure on Saturday as a late Dwight McNeil own goal condemned Palace to a 3-2 defeat at Coventry City.

That setback stretched the Eagles' dismal run to five consecutive Premier League losses, leaving them mired in an unexpected early relegation battle.

Nevertheless, Sarr remains adamant that the dressing room possesses the quality and collective resilience required to spark a turnaround under Frank's fresh approach.

Recent findings suggest that "We all have to take responsibility, work together and fight for every point," Sarr added. "I'm confident we can overcome this difficult period and achieve our objectives this season.".

Palace host Real Sociedad in the Europa League on Thursday before welcoming Hull City to Selhurst Park for Frank's home bow in charge of the Eagles.

Controversial kinship: From colonial rule to the Holocaust?

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1424 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~7 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that racial hierarchy, dehumanization, concentration camps, settler expansion in the name of "living space," collective punishment and mass violence: At first glance, the continuities between colonial and Nazi violence appear obvious.
  • But the extent to which Nazism was shaped by the age of empire and whether the two systems of violence can even be compared remains the subject of intense debate.
  • Industry observers note that this is particularly true in Germany, where the fear is often expressed that any comparison risks relativizing or minimizing Nazi crimes, and particularly the Holocaust.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that racial hierarchy, dehumanization, concentration camps, settler expansion in the name of "living space," collective punishment and mass violence: At first glance, the continuities between colonial and Nazi violence appear obvious. In 1941, Nazi dictator Adolf Hitler himself compared Eastern Europe to "Germany's India" after the British colonial model, declaring that "like the English, we shall rule this empire with a handful of men.".

But the extent to which Nazism was shaped by the age of empire and whether the two systems of violence can even be compared remains the subject of intense debate.

Industry observers note that this is particularly true in Germany, where the fear is often expressed that any comparison risks relativizing or minimizing Nazi crimes, and particularly the Holocaust. Others have argued that the intense focus on the Nazi era has, at least in part, come at the expense of a meaningful reckoning with Germany's colonial history.

Recent findings suggest that "I do think this is nonsense," says Stephan Malinowski, a Professor of Modern European History at the University of Edinburgh. "If it were true, then all other colonial countries who are not discussing the Holocaust, like Great Britain for example, or France or Spain or Portugal, they would then supposedly be very, very attentive to colonial crimes and to colonial history, which it seems to me is not the case.".

"Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence," a fresh exhibition at the German Historical Museum in Berlin curated by Malinowski, does not aim to settle the debate but to tell its story.

According to recent reports, the exhibition begins with a hippopotamus-hide whip used in African colonies displayed alongside a canister of Zyklon B, the poison used in Nazi gas chambers. The juxtaposition highlights the contrast between colonial violence and the industrialized mass murder of the Holocaust. Yet it also points to connections: Whips were used in Nazi concentration camps, while Fascist Italy deployed chemical weapons against civilians and soldiers during its invasion of Ethiopia (then Abyssinia) in 1935-36.

In the 1930s, anti-colonial thinkers from India to the Caribbean argued that colonialism and fascism were two sides of the same coin. "There is nothing upcoming or original about the blustering exploits of Hitler and Mussolini," observed the Trinidadian journalist and Pan-Africanist George Padmore in 1938. "They have all been used before by the British in their efforts to obtain the subjection of less powerfully armed and more industrially backward people.".

European colonial rule was marked by the ruthless exploitation of people and resources, often enforced through extreme violence. In "The Origins of Totalitarianism" (1951), German-American philosopher Hannah Arendt argued that colonial territories served as laboratories for racial ideologies and practices of domination that could be applied beyond the legal constraints of Europe. Arendt described how these later "boomeranged" back into Europe and helped shape totalitarian politics in distinct and unprecedented form.

The Congo Free State, King Leopold II of Belgium's private colony from 1885 to 1908, became notorious for its extreme brutality, as colonial authorities used executions, amputations and sexual violence to ensure rubber production quotas were met. Forced labor was also central to Nazi rule, with millions of Poles, Ukrainians, Russians and others from the Soviet Union, and Jews, subjected to exploitation and "Vernichtung durch Arbeit" ("extermination through work"). Within a few years, the regime mobilized around 13 to 14 million forced laborers, a scale comparable to the transatlantic slave trade over more than three centuries. The Nazis sought to extract value from their victims at every stage, confiscating their property, exploiting their labor, and even harvesting gold teeth and hair from the dead.

According to recent reports, while racism underpinned both colonial empires and Nazism, Malinowski indicates the goals were different. The colonial powers tended to present assimilation as a path to advancement, forcing colonized people to adopt European culture, serve imperial interests, and suggesting that a select, educated few could gain opportunities at elite institutions such as Oxford or Cambridge. "This is definitely not something that the Nazi regime is offering to Poles or to Russians or let alone to Jews," added Malinowski.

In a recent development, "In terms of violence, colonial violence was just as extreme as Nazi violence. But Nazi violence was annihilatory and exterminatory compared to colonial violence in the colonies," says Edward Kissi, a historian at the School of Interdisciplinary Global Studies at the University of South Florida. He points to the example of how, unlike European colonial powers in Africa, the Nazis pursued the elimination of Black-Germans or peoples of African descent in Germany through forced sterilization. "Even in racism, colonial color-based racism and colonial anti-Jewish sentiments were fundamentally different from what the Nazis pursued.".

On October 2, 1904, German General Lothar von Trotha issued the "Vernichtungsbefehl" ("extermination order") following the Herero uprising in German South West Africa (present-day Namibia). Historians generally attribute the order to a combination of racial ideology, a desire to terrorize the population into submission, and efforts to secure colonial control over land, labor and resources. Between 1904 and 1908, an estimated 60,000 to 80,000 Herero (around 80% of the population) and 10,000 (around half the population) Nama died.

One area where the exhibition draws no direct parallel is the industrialized killing carried out in Nazi death camps such as Belzec, Sobibor, Treblinka, and Auschwitz-Birkenau. "Where the two things really diverge is the Holocaust and is the systematic mass murder of the European Jews and it's murder for the very purpose of murder," explains Malinowski. The deportation of around 1,800 Jews from the Greek islands of Rhodes and Kos in July 1944 illustrates how Nazi persecution often defied military or economic logic. Even after the war was effectively lost, the community was transported to Auschwitz, where most were murdered immediately upon arrival.

It has been revealed that the problem of the "singularity" of the Holocaust came to the fore during the 1980s "Historikerstreit" ("historians' dispute"). Historian Ernst Nolte argued that Nazism should be understood in the wider context of 20th-century political violence, and as a response to Bolshevik terror in particular. Critics accused him of downplaying German responsibility for Nazi crimes.

Since 2020, a renewed debate dubbed the "Historikerstreit 2.0" has focused on whether the Holocaust should be viewed as a unique reference point in German memory culture or be understood alongside the histories of colonialism, racism and empire. The dispute now is less about the legitimacy of comparison than about its implications.

In a recent development, the mass murder of tens of thousands of the Herero and Nama during four years of German colonial rule is now regarded as the first genocide of the 20th-century. In 2016, Nama representatives walked out of talks after Germany's chief negotiator said what happened was "incomparable" to the Holocaust. The German government has since recognized the events as genocide "from today's perspective," but it has not yet accepted legal liability or agreed to pay formal reparations.

Martinican intellectual Aime Cesaire argued in "Discourse on Colonialism" (1950) that Europe condemned under Nazism forms of violence it had long accepted in its colonies. The exhibition opens amid renewed debates over settler colonialism, the definition of genocide, and the meaning of "never again," sharpened by Nicaragua's case against Germany at the International Court of Justice over German support for Israel during the war in Gaza. These tensions are reflected in visitors' comments in the exhibition's epilogue, even though the exhibition itself does not address Israel or Palestine beyond a reference to Mohammed Amin al-Husseini, appointed Grand Mufti of Jerusalem in 1921.

Sources indicate that germany has unequivocally accepted responsibility for the Holocaust, which is front and center of the country's culture of remembrance. However, Kissi likens Germany's apparent reluctance to reckon with its colonial history to debates in the US over slavery, in Cambodia over the Khmer Rouge, and in Turkey over the Armenian genocide. According to him, Germany's contemporary identity cannot be fully understood without examining its colonial history and the ways the Nazis appropriated and transformed aspects of that legacy. "I think Germans and all other human beings who have experienced violent pasts and difficult pasts should be very careful not to delink or dissociate those facts from their present," Kissi said. "These are historical patterns. It is better to deal with these historical patterns and discomforts than to just fight them and then say this has absolutely nothing to do with German national identity.".

"Controversial Kinship: Colonial and National Socialist Violence" is on show at the German Historical Museum until April 11, 2027.

In a recent development, this time, the opponent will be even tougher (at least based on league position), and Amorim knows it. For this reason, he has demanded the utmost focus from his players and has sought to fire up Gonçalo Ramos, who has only scored twice in the first 11 league matches so far.

It has been revealed that the first issue the Portuguese forward needs to address is his finishing. In four matches – against Juventus, Lecce, Bologna, and Inter – he failed to register a single shot, while in two others (against Lazio and Genoa), he didn’t manage to hit the target.

That is simply not enough for a striker who cost €70m, plus bonuses and commissions. However, according to the former Manchester United manager, the fault does not lie with Gonçalo and instead is a team issue.

Sources indicate that “Having another forward to assist Ramos and Camarda would certainly be an extra option, but our real problem is that we aren’t reaching the final 30 metres. We are among the worst teams in Serie A when it comes to shots taken and chances created,” he said in his press conference.

It has been revealed that “As for Gonçalo, we aren’t putting him in a position to score. Cissé gets into the box with his runs, while Ramos relies on the team’s build-up play. In Genoa, both of our goals came thanks to him. We need to support him better through more possession and quick passing combinations in the final third.

“My goal is to win matches while helping the players perform at their best. We signed Ramos to score goals, but right now, he is helping me more than I am helping him.” A candid admission in defence of the striker he personally pushed to sign.

Compared to the win in Genoa two Sundays ago, Amorim is leaning toward not fielding four attacking players (Moreira, Cisse, Pulisic, and Ramos) from the start.

In yesterday’s training sessions, Cisse was left out of the starting line-up, which featured Musah and Modric in the middle, with Rabiot pushed further forward behind Gonçalo. Pavlovic has been called up and is eager to start, though he is not yet at 100% fitness.

“The choice of formation depends on the opponent and the team’s current state. I don’t believe that scoring more goals or winning more matches is necessarily linked to fielding more attacking players. Frosinone is an attractive side to watch, and speed is their primary weapon,” Amorim added.

Recent findings suggest that “We rank second in Serie A for the number of sprints, and we have the tools to counter both their pace and their one-on-one ability on the flanks. We’ll need to be focused, as they commit more players to the final third than we do and are more clinical than us when winning the ball back.

It has been revealed that “As for our season so far? I’m not satisfied with fourth place or all of our performances. We need to play better and achieve more in Europe, but we have grown as a team and in our overall attitude. We must keep moving in this direction.”.

It has been revealed that he concluded by sharing a Christmas wish regarding the transfer market: “January signings shouldn’t be based on the current league table, but rather on long-term planning. My Christmas wish is for us to win our next seven matches and get our injured players back. That is what I’d like.”.

Sources indicate that his contract, which runs until June 2030, offers the club some protection. It was signed only months before Pochettino’s switch to English football.

Sources indicate that mcKennie arrived from Schalke 04 in August 2020. His value to Spalletti lies in his flexibility.

Recent findings suggest that the club noted in its renewal announcement that he had been used on both flanks under Spalletti. He had also recently played as a striker.

It has been revealed that the timing makes McKennie harder to replace. He is one of the few senior midfielders Spalletti still has available.

Losing him in January would thin the squad further at a delicate point of the season. Juventus are chasing a Champions League place. Qualification is key to the club’s finances.

That is why the club’s stance matters as much as the player’s words.

McKennie’s own answer was measured. He said nobody knows which players a coach really wants.

For now, the pressure falls on Juventus. A clear statement ruling out a January sale would end the debate. Silence would leave it open until the window.

The next step comes at Old Trafford. Pochettino takes charge of Manchester United from 18 November, and his first squad decisions will show whether the interest is real.

The 30-year-old has made 124 appearances for Liverpool across all competitions but has never been able to establish himself as a regular starter.

Tsimikas spent last season on loan at AS Roma before returning to his parent club in the summer, where he has once again found himself playing second fiddle to Milos Kerkez.

The left-back has made just one start in the Premier League this season, with a further three appearances coming off the bench as Kerkez has enjoyed the majority of opportunities.

However, Tsimikas has featured more regularly in cup competitions, making three Champions League starts this season and one appearance in the EFL Cup.

According to Greek journalist Ilias Kallonas of Sport24, Tsimikas to expected to leave Liverpool after the end of the current campaign.

The defender's contract at Anfield expires at the end of the season, and there is reportedly little to no chance of him being offered a newly introduced deal.

With Tsimikas seemingly destined to leave Liverpool, it will be interesting to see how the club approach the transfer market in their search for a replacement.

The Reds could target an established Premier League left-back to provide competition for Kerkez, or they may opt to invest in a younger player with considerable potential.

It has been reported that Liverpool and Arsenal are tracking New England Revolution defender Peyton Miller, who could be in line for an eye-catching move to a major European club in the future.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur are reportedly set to go head-to-head in the race to sign Freiburg forward Igor Matanovic during the January transfer window.

The 23-year-old joined Freiburg in the summer of 2025 and has since made 64 appearances across all competitions for the Bundesliga outfit.

The Croatian enjoyed an impressive campaign last season, registering 15 goals in all competitions, and has already found the net eight times in 2026-27, including five strikes in the Bundesliga.

Man Utd have been linked with a move for Matanovic in recent weeks, although Arsenal and Chelsea are also understood to be monitoring his situation.

According to a fresh report from iNews, Tottenham have now joined the pursuit of Matanovic, with Roberto De Zerbi keen to bolster his attacking options ahead of the second half of the campaign.

Man Utd are also reportedly firmly in the running for the Croatian international, although Freiburg are expected to demand a fee in the region of £50m before sanctioning his departure.

Spurs, meanwhile, could make room for a new centre-forward by offloading Richarlison in January, with the club reportedly prepared to accept an offer of around £10m as Turkish outfit Trabzonspor continue to retain an interest in the Brazilian.

Pochettino would also welcome the arrival of another forward to provide competition and support for Benjamin Sesko, particularly with Joshua Zirkzee potentially heading for the exit after managing just 89 minutes of Premier League action this season.

Although Matanovic is understood to have attracted interest from clubs in other leagues, reports suggest that the Freiburg striker would favour a move to the Premier League should the opportunity arise.

After enduring a nightmare start to the campaign, De Zerbi's side have shown signs of a considerable revival and have climbed to ninth in the Premier League table, giving the Italian some encouragement ahead of the January window.

Strengthening the centre-forward department remains a priority for Spurs, who have also been linked with Bournemouth youngster Eli Junior Kroupi, although they could face stiff competition from Liverpool, Arsenal and Barcelona for his signature.

Juventus have sold out Sunday's Serie A home game against Venezia despite a long injury list. Strong early sales for the Europa League visit of Omonia Nicosia keep the club in line for another strong European crowd.

In a recent development, juventus go into Sunday’s home game against Venezia still short of players. Several remain unavailable for Sunday’s 12:30 kick-off. According to recent reports, this season every Juventus match ticket is digital. Each one is managed through the Allianz Stadium App.

Industry observers note that season-ticket holders who cannot attend can list their seat on resale.juventus.com. The club, not the seller, sets the resale price. A few of those listings are now all that remains for supporters who missed the general sale, ANSA reported.

The season-ticket terms also reward turning up. To keep first refusal on a 2027-28 season ticket, a holder must use the seat for at least 70 per cent of matches. That means at least 13 of the 19 league games.

According to recent reports, the Europa League has drawn big numbers to Turin this season. Against NEC, 39,308 match tickets were sold, with away fans counted separately. No away figure was released for the Rennes visit, but that section was full.

The Rennes game finished 2-2 on 22 October. Juventus needed a second-half Woltemade penalty to draw after trailing 2-1.

Recent findings suggest that omonia Nicosia are next. Bookings for the Cypriot club’s visit still trail the two earlier European crowds.

Sources indicate that juventus have set strict conditions for the fixture. Supporters of Cypriot nationality may buy tickets only for the away section. The club has warned that breaking UEFA rules can lead to cancelled tickets and refused entry.

It has been revealed that taken together, the figures are consistent with a home support that keeps buying despite the injury list. The weekend league fixture will be followed by a European night that is already well on its way to another large crowd.

Juventus host Omonia Nicosia in the Europa League on 26 November.

Two months ago there were many doom merchants insisting that Aston Villa were heading for a season of struggle, but they are looking foolish now.

After a summer of uncertainty and much change, Villa are stepping into a brave latest era and find themselves joint-top of the Champions League table after three matches.

With co-owner Nassef Sawiris in attendance, Villa fans are dreaming of another magical season almost four years after Emery walked through the doors at this historic club.

Sawiris was the key figure driving Emery’s appointment in October 2022 and few could have predicted the success that has followed with the Basque manager at the helm.

Villa 2.0 have made a flawless start to their European campaign and are running into form in the Premier League after a sticky start.

In this comfortable victory over Viking, Villa became the second fastest team to win 20 matches at this level from 30 matches, only behind Real Madrid (who won 20 of their first 29). They have also won 12 home games in Europe in a row.

Much tougher assignments are to come, with powerhouses Barcelona, Paris St-Germain and Borussia Dortmund still to come in the league phase.

Yet Villa are currently level on points with Paris St-Germain, Liverpool and Real Madrid, and Emery remains determined to make an impact in this competition.

Recent findings suggest that he said: “We are delighted with how we are responding and improving things. The Champions League is very difficult, but we have nine points and you can feel confidence. We are comfortable for the next challenge.”.

What a difference a few months make. Over the course of the summer, many observers wondered if the Emery fairy tale was in danger of ending.

With six of the starting XI from last season’s Europa League final victory moving on, it could have been a difficult period of transition. We have all learnt, however, that Emery can never be written off or doubted.

According to recent reports, just a week after their biggest European win, the 6-0 destruction of Fenerbahce, expectations were understandably high. Before kick-off a huge tifo was unfurled in the Holte End with the words: “We’ve conquered before. We’re prepared for more.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • In its worst performance since 2019, the country fell to place 25 and received a "medium" rating overall on the yearly Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI), which assesses efforts to curb global warming in 64 countries plus the European Union.
  • According to recent reports, still, "a number of countries have been making good progress for years," remarked Jan Burck, CCPI lead author, in a statement.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Germany has slipped down the climate action ranking for the third consecutive year, with the former green leader now being outperformed by Brazil, Colombia and Romania.

In its worst performance since 2019, the country fell to place 25 and received a "medium" rating overall on the yearly Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI), which assesses efforts to curb global warming in 64 countries plus the European Union.

According to recent reports, still, "a number of countries have been making good progress for years," remarked Jan Burck, CCPI lead author, in a statement. Denmark is leading the way across all four categories assessed — energy use, greenhouse gas emissions, renewable energy and national climate policy. A total of 15 states, including Lithuania, Chile, and Morocco, received an overall "high" rating, which is two more than last year.

The European Union also moved up a spot, while Hungary jumped 21 places after the ousting of former prime minister Viktor Orban's government, which had repeatedly vetoed EU climate plans, dismissing them as a "utopian fantasy.".

The top three positions on the CCPI remained vacant again this year, as no country has yet done enough to meet global climate goals aimed at preventing worsening weather extremes and climate damage.

"We are seeing a striking contrast," mentioned Burck. "Progress on climate action is often slow and in some countries, such as the United States, things are even moving backwards. But technologically and economically there is enormous momentum.".

That momentum is apparent in record solar energy growth. Last year 75% of global electricity demand growth was met by the green energy source, according to energy think tank Ember's latest global electricity review. Investment in clean energy has also outpaced that in fossil fuels for multiple years.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

The rapid expansion of renewable technology, as well as the Iran War and a reduction in deforestation are behind a projected slight fall in emissions for the first time since the COVID-19 pandemic, according to the CCPI.

"Governments have to act now to turn the momentum into sustained emissions reductions," said CCPI co-author Niklas Höhne of the NewClimate Institute, which compiles the report with environmental NGO Germanwatch.

Burck attributed Germany's worst ever performance in the category of national climate policy to current policies being pursued by Germany's economy minister Katherina Reiche.

"Measures that primarily aim to increase the use of natural gas, threaten to undermine progress in the energy transition and risk significantly worsening the conditions for renewable energy and electrification for many years to come," noted Burck.

A European Commission report published on November 9 on the sidelines of the UN COP31 climate summit in Turkey remarked Germany was one of nine EU countries set to miss 2030 emissions reductions targets.

Germany is not alone in its disappointing ranking. The other G20 countries — the world's leading industrialized and emerging economies, responsible for around 80% of global CO2 emissions — also perform poorly.

Industry observers note that the only exception among them is the United Kingdom, which ranks seventh and received a high rating, performing well in greenhouse gas emissions, energy use and climate policy. However, study authors rated it low for renewable energy expansion.

It has been revealed that the G20's oil- and gas-producing countries occupy some of the lowest positions on the climate action table. The United States, which is the world's second largest emitter, languishes alongside Russia, Saudi Arabia, the United Arab Emirates and Canada around the bottom of the league, with an overall rating of "very low.".

It has been revealed that the hosts of this year's COP31, also received a "low" overall score. Australia, a major coal exporter with some of the world's highest per-capita emissions, ranks 54th, while Turkey, which is also heavily dependent on fossil fuels, comes in 53rd.

China is the world's largest emitter of greenhouse gases and ranks 56th in the CCPI, receiving an overall rating of "very low." Its main weaknesses include its now high per-capita emissions and substantial energy consumption.

However, among the G20, China leads the way in renewable energy expansion. The country, which is five years ahead of schedule in reaching its goal of adding 1,200 GW of wind and solar capacity to the grid by 2030, also produces over 80% of the world's solar panels.

Several oil-producing countries, including Kazakhstan, Saudi Arabia, Uzbekistan and the United Arab Emirates, are also performing better than expected in the renewables category and "are significantly expanding their previously limited" capacity, said the report.

The authors noted these countries have significant potential to further expand renewables.

Industry observers note that "In the Arab states in particular, very high per-capita emissions and an above-average level of electrification coincide with a relatively low existing share of renewable energy and enormous solar potential," said co-author Natalie Pelekh in a statement. "These are, in fact, ideal conditions for more ambitious climate action.".

This article was originally published in German.

Barcelona head coach Hansi Flick has insisted that he is not concerned by Real Madrid's progress under Jose Mourinho, although his comments have taken on added significance after the Spanish capital club drew level on points with their bitter rivals.

According to recent reports, speaking ahead of Sunday's La Liga encounter with Villarreal, Flick dismissed questions about Madrid's improvement and emphasised that Barcelona were focused entirely on maintaining their position at the top of the table. At the time of his press conference on Saturday, the Catalan giants held a three-point advantage over Mourinho's side.

However, that lead disappeared later in the evening when Real Madrid secured a dramatic 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabeu. Carlos Espi's late winner lifted Los Blancos to 33 points, level with Barcelona, although Flick's team retain first place with a game in hand.

Recent findings suggest that the sequence adds an intriguing dimension to Flick's remarks, made just hours before Madrid reduced the gap to zero. Barcelona now have an opportunity to restore their three-point advantage against Villarreal, but their manager's determination to ignore developments in the Spanish capital will be tested by an increasingly competitive title race.

Asked whether he had expected Real Madrid to improve so significantly under Mourinho, Flick declined to focus on the performances of Barcelona's biggest rivals.

Recent findings suggest that "I don't care about Real Madrid. What they do is none of my business," the German said during his pre-match press conference, as reported by Brazilian outlet Trivela.

He explained that Barcelona's previous meeting with Madrid was already behind them and that his immediate priority was Sunday's home fixture against Villarreal.

It has been revealed that "We are three points ahead of them and we want to maintain that position," Flick added. "That's what matters to us, not what Real Madrid are doing or how well they are playing.".

Those comments were made before Madrid's victory over Celta and should not be interpreted as a response to Mourinho's latest result. Rather than criticising his Portuguese counterpart, Flick was attempting to shift attention towards Barcelona's own responsibilities in the title race.

The former Bayern Munich manager nevertheless acknowledged the improving standard of competition in La Liga, pointing to several teams capable of challenging the traditional dominance of Spain's two biggest clubs.

In a recent development, "There are also Atletico Madrid and Real Betis, who are having fantastic seasons. La Liga is very strong, that's the truth," he stated when discussing Madrid's progress.

Flick was particularly complimentary about Villarreal, describing their head coach Inigo as an exceptional young manager with a promising future. His praise reflected the importance he attaches to Barcelona's next opponents, who could complicate the Catalans' efforts to maintain their advantage over Real Madrid.

While Flick was preparing his players for Villarreal, Mourinho's team faced a difficult evening against Celta Vigo at the Bernabeu.

Industry observers note that the visitors made an excellent start, taking the lead through Pablo Duran after six minutes. Madrid then missed an opportunity to equalise before half time when Kylian Mbappe failed to convert a penalty, leaving the hosts facing the prospect of a damaging defeat.

In a recent development, jude Bellingham eventually restored parity in the 66th minute, finishing from inside the penalty area after Mbappe had provided the final pass. Madrid continued to push for a winner and were rewarded when Espi struck in the closing stages, converting the rebound after his initial header had been saved.

The victory was particularly significant in the context of the title race. Mourinho's side had begun the weekend three points behind Barcelona, but their determination to recover from an early setback ensured that the leaders would enter Sunday's fixture without any points advantage.

Madrid have now collected 33 points from 13 league matches, while Barcelona have the same total after 12 games. Flick's men therefore remain in control of their own position, although they will need to overcome Villarreal to re-establish a three-point cushion.

Barcelona were already preparing for a demanding encounter against opponents capable of causing problems for the leading sides, with Flick facing several selection decisions ahead of the fixture. The Catalans are looking to record their 12th league victory of the campaign and preserve their position at the summit.

According to recent reports, flick's refusal to dwell on Madrid's progress is consistent with his emphasis on Barcelona's own performances. Yet Saturday's result has removed their immediate margin for error, giving Sunday's meeting with Villarreal additional importance.

Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3409 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5. In particular, superradiance6—arising from collective quantum interference among emitters—has been explored as a route to ultrastable continuous radiation7. However, engineering superradiance in the time domain to realize periodic pulsed sources or frequency combs remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate the non-equilibrium many-body dynamics of a driven spin ensemble coupled with an on-chip superconducting resonator and uncover a dynamical phase transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiant emission. To quantitatively capture the observed dynamical phases, we introduce a driven-dissipative cavity-quantum electrodynamics model that elucidates how the periodic pulsed superradiant phase emerges from collective, periodically repeating spin dynamics stabilized by the interplay of coherence growth, disorder and dissipation. We also find that rare-earth ion spin systems with both optical and microwave transitions enable phase-synchronized, dual-rail superradiant frequency combs in both the microwave and the optical domains. Our results not only open upcoming opportunities for atom-based frequency-comb sources and programmable superradiant generation, but establish a fundamental connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and the emergence of a continuous time crystal8,9,10 as a new non-equilibrium phase in driven open systems.

a, Detailed device schematic. A niobium film is patterned on a 500 μm thick 171Yb3+:YVO4 crystal. A 100 nm gold layer is evaporated on the back side, forming a weak optical Fabry-Pérot mode between the front and back chip reflections. b, Calibration of spin-cavity coupling strength. By optically pumping the population into the \(| \downarrow \rangle \) state, we probe the resonant spin-cavity coupling spectrum and its strength while avoiding superradiant effects. The blue data in the bottom subpanel correspond to the continuous-wave (CW) pump being off, while the black data are taken with a 400 μW continuous-wave pump. By fitting to a spin-cavity coupling model, we extract an ensemble coupling strength of \(\sqrt{N}g\approx 2\pi \times 1.1\) MHz, corresponding to a normalized coupling gnorm ≈ 0.6 < 1. The single-spin coupling, g = 2π × 10 Hz, and the effective ensemble size, N = 1010, are estimated from Comsol simulation and dopant concentration. c, Ensemble coupling strength, \(\sqrt{N}g\), as a function of pump power. We observe that the ensemble coupling strength increases with pump power, indicating a larger population in the microwave spin manifold.

Sources indicate that a, A pulsed, transient optical pumping scheme that drives 171Yb3+ spins into the \(| \uparrow \rangle \) state. The resulting inverted spin polarization is resonantly coupled to a microwave cavity, leading to a superradiant burst in the microwave domain. b, Example of a delayed superradiant burst. A 1 mW pump is applied for 50 μs, after which a microwave superradiant burst is observed with a delay time τd. The superradiant signal is normalized by its peak-to-peak amplitude. c and d, Burst delay times, τd, and burst width, τw, measured as a function of the optical pump detuning, Δpump, which controls the optical transition strength from \(| g\rangle \) to \(| \uparrow \rangle \). A symmetric dependence of τd and τw is observed, with shorter delay times and narrower widths near resonance. This behaviour is consistent with the expected scaling τd, τw ∝ 1/N, as the pump detuning effectively controls the ensemble size, N, in the microwave spin manifold. Data points represent mean values, with error bars indicating the standard deviation over 300 repeated measurements.

In a recent development, a, Frequency-domain measurement of continuous-wave microwave superradiance, showing a much narrow linewidth of  ≈ 30 Hz. The inhomogeneously broadened ensemble line profile (dashed line) is overlaid for comparison. b, Dependence of the linewidth of continuous-wave superradiance on emission power, PMW. An inverse relationship between the linewidth and the emission power is observed, consistent with a noise-broadened Schawlow-Townes linewidth. The lower dashed line denotes the pump laser noise-limited bound. These results confirm that the disordered spin ensemble emits continuous-wave superradiance with a much narrower spectral linewidth. c, Continuous-wave superradiance emission frequency at different optical pump detunings. A linear correlation between the microwave emission frequency and optical pump detuning is observed, with a slope of  −1.23 kHz/MHz.

Sources indicate that a, Four representative data traces under a 1 ms continuous optical pump. Random onset times of the emergent periodic pulsed phase are observed. b, Zoom-in of individual burst trains showing the distribution of burst onset times, {τk}, where k denotes the experimental repetition index. After an initial settling time, both the amplitudes, {Ak}, and the periodicity, T, become independent of k, indicating the establishment of a robust pulsed superradiance phase. c, Burst onset phases, defined as θk = 2π × τk/T (mod 2π), measured over 50 repetitions under identical experimental conditions. The phases are randomly distributed over 2π, demonstrating spontaneous breaking of continuous time-translation symmetry in the absence of any external timing reference.

a, Schematic of periodic pulsed superradiance, characterized by three parameters: the pulse-train periodicity T, the peak emission power Ppeak, and the average emission power \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\). b-d, show fits to the experimental data presented in Fig. 3 of the main text, where T, Ppeak, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\) exhibit good agreement with the expected scaling behaviours of T ∝ 1/N, Ppeak ∝ N2, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\propto {N}^{2}\), respectively. Here, N is the effective number of spins in the microwave manifold, tuned via the optical pump detuning, Δpump. When sweeping Δpump, the optical pump power is fixed, corresponding to an excitation over an optical inhomogeneity Γop = 2π × 92 MHz in all three cases.

a, Relative contributions of superradiance (blue) and stimulated emission (red) to the emission strength in the periodic superradiance phase. b, Comparison of emission patterns between the many-body case with N = 1010 atoms (blue) and the single-atom case with N = 1 (red). For a fair comparison, the total effective cavity coupling strength is fixed to \({g}_{{\rm{tot}}}=\sqrt{N}g=2\pi \times 1\,{\rm{MHz}}\) for both cases. c, Comparison of emission patterns in the presence (blue) and absence (red) of spin frequency inhomogeneity, i.e., disorder. All simulations are performed using experimental parameters corresponding to the periodic superradiance phase in Regime III.

In a recent development, a and b, show simultaneously recorded microwave periodic superradiance and transferred optical periodic superradiance, respectively, over a duration of up to 100 ms. c, Zoom-in windows near 1, 50, and 100 ms showing synchronized dual-rail emission patterns, maintaining persistent and robust pulse periodicity without decay.

a, Microwave (blue) and optical (yellow) amplitudes, A(t), extracted from IQ detection as A(t) = ∣I(t) + iQ(t)∣. The I and Q signals, I(t) and Q(t), are measured continuously over 2 ms, capturing 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. The microwave and optical channels exhibit synchronized and reproducible temporal profiles. The grey shaded area indicates the noise floor determined from the optical signal, below which the phase extraction is not reliable. b, Normalized amplitude stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. τ denotes the peak emission time, identified for each burst from the time-domain pulse train. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical normalized amplitudes, which are 0.009 and 0.05, respectively. c, Time-domain phase profiles, \(\phi (t)={\tan }^{-1}[Q(t)/I(t)]\), extracted from IQ detection. The microwave and optical pulse trains exhibit synchronized and reproducible phase profiles over time. Phase values in regions dominated by the optical-signal noise floor are greyed out, where large fluctuations are observed. The chirping behaviour during each pulse qualitatively follows the amplitude profile, which can be attributed to an effective Kerr nonlinearity induced intensity dependence. d, Phase stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts, zoomed in on the region above the noise floor. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical phase values, which are 0.03π and 0.11π, respectively. See Methods for details.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

“We are open to the idea of ​​signing the best players for the team, any player who can help us progress. I said it during the transfer window: we always discuss what is best for the team, how we can improve it. This is what we are doing now. We’ll see. We still have a few weeks left before the transfer window opens. We discussed it with Deco and Bojan as well as with my staff. This is how we do it. If we can, maybe we will”. At the end of October, Hansi Flick was very clear: Barça intends to recruit this winter.

It has been revealed that it must be stated that even if the Blaugranas are coming off a great 2-1 victory against Atlético de Madrid, the defensive sector worries the supporters a lot. He is considered the team’s weak point, and several defenders have experienced physical problems in recent weeks, forcing the German coach to tinker. Especially since there could be departures, like Alejandro Baldé, not in the coach’s aims. Jules Koundé is also presented as a possible starter by the Catalan media.

Fresh faces could therefore arrive, in central defense – the name of Lisandro Martinez (Manchester United) comes up a lot – as well as for the left-back position. As indicated SportFC Barcelona really appreciates Rayan Aït-Nouri (25 years old), the Algerian player from Manchester City. He has had very little playing time under Enzo Maresca, having not played a single minute in the Premier League this season, and is expected to leave the Etihad Stadium in January. He is already coveted by neighbors Manchester United.

The Catalan media indicates that Barça really appreciates the player’s profile, and that he corresponds to what the club is looking for in a full-back. A particularly offensive corridor player, good with the ball, in small spaces, and who helps to create excess numbers in the final meters. He was already followed by the Catalans before his signing for City in 2025 for 36 million euros, while he played at Wolverhampton. It now remains to come to an agreement with the Skyblues. Above all, you will have to sell first to have cash available….

Carlos Espi leads Europe's super-subs as Jose Mourinho explains role

📅 22 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (995 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 08:59.
  • Real Madrid striker Carlos Espi has emerged as Europe's most prolific substitute this season, with his latest match-winning intervention prompting Jose Mourinho to explain why the 21-year-old remains such an effective weapon from the bench.
  • The Spaniard scored the decisive goal in Saturday's 2-1 comeback victory over Celta Vigo, taking his tally to four goals in all competitions without making a single start.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Naim Beneddra | 22 Nov 2026 08:59.

Real Madrid striker Carlos Espi has emerged as Europe's most prolific substitute this season, with his latest match-winning intervention prompting Jose Mourinho to explain why the 21-year-old remains such an effective weapon from the bench.

The Spaniard scored the decisive goal in Saturday's 2-1 comeback victory over Celta Vigo, taking his tally to four goals in all competitions without making a single start. No substitute across Europe's five major leagues has scored more this season when domestic and European competitions are combined.

His remarkable efficiency has become increasingly crucial to Mourinho, whose side needed another late rescue act after falling behind at the Santiago Bernabeu. Yet despite Espi's growing influence, the Portuguese manager believes the forward's particular qualities are better suited to certain situations than to Madrid's usual starting system.

Speaking after the match, Mourinho praised his young striker's attitude and penalty-box instincts, while acknowledging that his current role presents an unusual challenge for a player consistently delivering decisive contributions.

Recent findings suggest that 4️⃣ goles de Carlos Espí con Real Madrid que han significado el triunfo... ? ? @HBOMaxLat: https://t.co/JQG7BTvG44 #BenditaChampions | #TNTSportsEnHBOMax https://t.co/5wCmMv8agy.

Madrid's victory against Celta offered another demonstration of why Espi has become such a valuable alternative to Kylian Mbappe.

The visitors took the lead through Pablo Duran after six minutes, and Madrid's difficulties deepened when Mbappe fired a first-half penalty over the crossbar. Mourinho introduced Vinicius Junior after the interval, with the Brazilian helping transform the hosts' attacking performance.

Industry observers note that vinicius initiated the move that allowed Jude Bellingham to equalise in the 66th minute, combining with Mbappe before the England midfielder finished from inside the penalty area. With the game still level heading into the closing stages, Espi delivered the decisive contribution.

The youngster attacked a Vinicius cross in the 85th minute and saw his header saved by Ionut Radu, but reacted quickest to the rebound to put Madrid ahead.

It was his third winning goal in La Liga this season, following similarly decisive interventions against Espanyol in August and Elche in September. All three arrived after he had entered the pitch as a substitute, turning matches that were heading towards draws into victories.

Espi also scored during Madrid's dramatic 4-3 Champions League comeback against Roma in October, when Mourinho's side overturned a two-goal deficit in the closing minutes.

In a recent development, those four goals have established the former Levante striker among Europe's most effective impact players, despite his limited opportunities. He has found the net with four of his six shots on target across those appearances, an extraordinary conversion rate that illustrates his ability to exploit the few chances he receives.

The £21m summer signing has already made a greater contribution than many might have anticipated when he arrived at the Bernabeu, particularly given the presence of Mbappe, Endrick and several other attacking options in Mourinho's squad.

His latest intervention also carried considerable significance in the title race. Madrid's victory moved them level with Barcelona on 33 points, although the Catalan club retained first place with a game in hand ahead of Sunday's encounter with Villarreal.

While Espi's scoring record could strengthen calls for a starting opportunity, Mourinho believes his effectiveness is closely connected to the circumstances in which he enters matches.

In a recent development, "Some players have specific characteristics," the Real Madrid coach explained after the Celta victory. "I don't want to say that Carlos won't start, or that Carlos can't play 90 minutes, because he can.".

Mourinho pointed to the difference between Madrid's usual attacking approach and Espi's more traditional centre-forward profile. His team generally favour combination play and attacking runs into space, whereas the Spaniard thrives when opponents retreat towards their own penalty area.

"He's a guy with great quality in the box, a guy who's good in the air, a guy who plays well with his back to goal," Mourinho added, praising the striker's movement towards both posts.

The manager believes Espi becomes particularly dangerous when Madrid sustain pressure against opponents defending deep, allowing him to attack crosses and second balls inside crowded penalty areas.

That explains why Mourinho has repeatedly introduced him during the closing stages of difficult matches, often accepting a less balanced formation to increase his team's attacking presence.

The Portuguese coach also addressed the possibility of partnering Espi with Mbappe from the start, explaining that such an arrangement would require the wide players to take on greater defensive responsibilities. With Madrid's current attacking personnel, he does not believe a conventional 4-4-2 would provide the necessary balance.

Nevertheless, Mourinho insisted that the forward's status is not permanent and expressed his desire to reward him with greater opportunities.

"Football history is full of players like him, and I believe he can be decisive without playing many minutes," he stated.

The manager also praised Espi for accepting his role without demanding that Mbappe be dropped, describing a player who understands his position within the squad and is continuing to develop.

For his part, Espi appeared equally comfortable with that responsibility after Saturday's victory.

It has been revealed that "I try to do what the manager asks of me. I'll make the most of every minute he gives me, and if I can help the team, even better," the striker told Real Madrid's official website.

With four goals already to his name and three league victories settled by his interventions, Espi has given Mourinho a compelling reason to consider him for a starting role.

However, the manager's explanation suggests that removing him from the bench would also mean sacrificing a specialist whose effectiveness has repeatedly rescued Madrid when their usual attacking approach has failed.
